summary: Set up Security Champions onboarding automation: Jira project + Confluence space + Slack channel provisioning
description:
Issue summary:
Request to provision a repeatable onboarding/offboarding automation for Redwood's new Security Champions program. Goal is a single self-service flow that creates the required project-level artifacts and assigns role-based permissions when a user is added to the Okta group 'sec-champs'.

Background: 
The Security Org is launching a Security Champions track across product teams. Current manual steps (create Jira access, add Confluence space membership, create per-pod Slack channel, and grant repo permissions) are error-prone and slow. We want a supported internal pattern that ties into our existing SSO/SCIM provisioning and central automation tooling.

Impact: 
- Faster, auditable onboarding for program participants (expected 40–60 new champions in first quarter).
- Reduce manual tickets to internal-support and avoid inconsistent permissions that have caused access gaps in past pilots.

Request details:
1) Jira: create a small team project key SEC-CHAMP (team-managed) with a project role 'Champion' and an auditable Jira group 'sec-champ-members'. Configure project permissions so 'Champion' role can comment, create tasks, and view roadmaps. Add an automation rule: when a user is added to 'sec-champ-members' group, add them to the project role and create a welcome task assigned to them.
2) Confluence: provision a 'Security Champions' space with an onboarding template and a permissions scheme that grants view/edit to 'sec-champ-members' group and read-only to 'security-engineering' group. Enable space-level analytics and set space watchers to security-leads.
3) Slack: create a private org-wide channel #sec-champ-announcements and an automated per-pod private channel naming pattern (e.g., #sec-champs-pod-<pod-name>) created when a pod owner enrolls their pod. Automate membership: add user to #sec-champ-announcements and their pod channel based on Okta group mapping.
4) Automation/integration: use Okta SCIM group 'sec-champs' as the source of truth. Implement automation using existing org automation runner (CI job + AWS Lambda) or Jira automation + Slack workflow + Confluence REST API. Ensure offboarding removes users from all artifacts and logs actions to the infra-audit log.
5) Acceptance criteria: a) adding a test user to Okta 'sec-champs' results in (within 15 minutes) membership in Jira group, Confluence space access, addition to #sec-champ-announcements, and creation of Jira welcome task; b) removing the user reverses access; c) actions are logged in central audit; d) docs page and runbook created in Confluence with troubleshooting steps.

Timeline request: staged rollout with dev/testing in staging in 5 business days, production enablement within 10 business days after sign-off.

Additional notes: include scope for per-pod owners to request/approve pod channel creation. We want minimal manual steps for SRE/Security team once automation is active.
